@copilot Update this PR directly to simplify the Spring RMI metric test assertions in instrumentation/spring/spring-rmi-4.0/javaagent/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/spring/rmi/v4_0/SpringRmiTest.java, following the explicit RPC metric assertion style in instrumentation/apache-dubbo-2.7/testing/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/apachedubbo/v2_7/AbstractDubboTest.java. This is a test-only refactor, not a telemetry behavior change.

Replace the generic assertMetrics and assertDurationMetrics machinery with explicit waitAndAssertMetrics assertions beside the operations in the success, exception, and inherited/overloaded tests. Use explicit client/server metric names and hasPointsSatisfying point lambdas. Write expected attributes directly with hasAttributesSatisfyingExactly and equalTo. Remove the dynamic lists of histogram point assertion consumers, method-string splitting, Attributes.builder, and Map<Attributes, Long> count calculation. Prefer a little repetition over helpers that calculate expected telemetry. Existing unrelated trace assertion code is outside this refactor.

In the inherited/overloaded test, explicitly expect three preview points for each role. In rpc/dup mode, explicitly expect three legacy client points, but two legacy server points: service springrmi.app.SpringRmiGreeterImpl with method inherited and count 1, and the same service with method overloaded and count 2. Both overloaded calls aggregate into that legacy server point. Keep the concrete service/method values and counts visible in the assertions.

Preserve every existing metric assertion and scenario other than its structural refactoring: legacy-only mode remains metric-free; preview metrics use seconds; dual-mode legacy metrics use milliseconds; retain counts, existing positive-duration assertions, exact attributes, success and failure coverage, inherited and overloaded interface identities. Continue asserting server metrics only for the RMI test source. Gate legacy metric assertions inside preview-enabled dual mode, not merely on emitOldRpcSemconv, since default legacy-only mode emits no metrics. Do not reintroduce bucket-boundary assertions or weaken expected telemetry to simplify the test.

Leave production code, preview gating, metadata, shared metrics code/tests, and other modules unchanged. Remove unused imports. Run the module's narrowest spotlessApply directly before its existing default, preview, and dual-mode tests, and report actual validation blockers. Check the final diff changes assertion structure only. Preserve the PR's base and draft/ready state. Do not create another PR or edit its title or description.

replies.body: Replaced the generic metric helpers with explicit per-test client/server metric assertions and preserved default-mode absence and `/dup` legacy coverage. Commit: `06d851a9`. Spotless and all three Spring RMI test modes passed.

threads.body: [General] Both no-argument metric factories select generic buckets that omit boundaries recommended by the selected [v1.44.0 RPC metric conventions](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.44.0/docs/rpc/rpc-metrics.md), reducing latency resolution—for example, combining the recommended 100–250 ms and 250–500 ms buckets. Pass the recommended boundaries through `get(List<Double>)` for both client and server metrics, or document a concrete reason for departing from that recommendation. The same issue occurs in `RpcServerMetrics.get()` at line 72.

replies.body: These defaults deliberately follow the revised general RPC bucket recommendation in [open-telemetry/semantic-conventions#4185](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/pull/4185), merged October 21 and adopted by the shared factories in [#20883](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20883). The existing 13 boundaries match that recommendation exactly. Switching Spring RMI back to the older v1.44.0 list would undo that adoption, so no change is needed here.

@copilot Update this PR directly so Spring RMI adds only the new RPC duration metrics, never legacy metrics. Spring RMI had no legacy RPC metrics before this PR, so there is no legacy metric behavior to preserve in rpc/dup. This user-directed change supersedes the earlier requests in this PR to retain legacy metric emission and assertions.

Required behavior: with RPC preview disabled, emit no Spring RMI metrics; with preview rpc or rpc/dup, emit rpc.client.call.duration and, for the RMI server path, rpc.server.call.duration in seconds. Neither mode should emit rpc.client.duration or rpc.server.duration, or other newly introduced legacy RPC metrics, for scope io.opentelemetry.spring-rmi-4.0. Preserve existing span semantics, including dual-mode legacy span attributes, errors, propagation, interface/method identity, preview gating, default enablement, and histogram advice.

The no-argument RpcClientMetrics.get() and RpcServerMetrics.get() factories currently honor emitOld in dual mode. Correct production registration/metric construction as well as the tests; merely deleting old assertions is not sufficient. Reuse shared metric machinery rather than duplicating listeners. If explicit per-registration support in the shared factories is needed, make the smallest compatible change and keep existing callers' defaults and dual-emission behavior unchanged. Do not override global or instance semconv configuration to force preview-only, add a user-facing configuration setting, or filter metrics at export. Remove Spring RMI's now-unnecessary metrics dual-emission context customizers and their associated imports/deprecation suppressions where no longer needed.

Keep the newly explicit per-test assertions in SpringRmiTest. Remove the old millisecond metric assertion blocks, keep default metric absence and new metric checks for success/failure, inherited methods, overloads, exact attributes, existing positive sums, counts, and client/server distinctions. Verify legacy Spring RMI metric absence in both preview and dual test modes after the operations complete. Keep three preview points per role in the overload test. Add focused shared-helper coverage if its behavior is extended, including preservation of existing dual-emission callers. Do not reintroduce bucket checks into instrumentation tests. The shared bucket defaults intentionally implement the revised recommendation adopted in #20883 from open-telemetry/semantic-conventions#4185; leave them unchanged.

Keep this change scoped to Spring RMI and any necessary compatible shared metric support/tests, not native Java RMI, GWT, or unrelated instrumentations. Run the narrowest relevant spotlessApply directly before focused shared tests if changed and the existing Spring RMI default/preview/dual tests; report actual blockers. Preserve this PR's base and draft/ready state. Do not create another PR or edit its title or description.
